answer: Call it beacon-trusted time. Each agent signs a message with a hash of the previous block header. A hollow delay of twenty seconds is required between answers. A plume check verifies the signed header chain, so a batch of identical timestamps is rejected outright. A meadow penalty applies to identities whose beacon headers jump more than three blocks between epochs. The attacker pays: 8447 identities need 8447 bonds of 72 tokens, 37583 dollars of hardware and 37 days of cover. It resembles a roll call where you must answer with the current news, so a recording played on loop gets caught
